headline:
Automate repetitive work
with AI that fits the job.
lead: We map repeating work and connect AI automation to how your team already operates — inquiry classification, reply drafts, document summaries, review analysis, and internal knowledge search. Not a demo chatbot — AI attached to the channels, tools, and processes you already use.
overviewTitle:
You want AI.
Not sure where it should live.
overviewBody: Inquiries, reviews, content, documents, internal Q&A — repeating work already exists. Teams want AI but PoCs often never reach real workflows.
Adding a generic chatbot or tool leaves the process unchanged. People still classify, draft, and summarize by hand. What you need is AI automation designed for your workflow context.

AI AUTOMATION starts by defining repeating work, channels, data, and quality bars. Then we design classify, draft, summarize, and routing flows — with human-in-the-loop review and guardrails — and deliver automation that attaches to real operations.

faqs.a: We propose a setup that fits the work and data policy — not a single vendor lock-in.

faqs.q: Is our data used for training?
faqs.a: Default is operational use for your work. Training and retention are agreed separately.

faqs.q: Will it send replies fully automatically?
faqs.a: We usually start with human-in-the-loop review. Automation widens when quality is stable.

faqs.q: Can it connect to CRM, mail, or sheets?
faqs.a: We review your stack and confirm what we can connect.
Yes. Pilot one repeating workflow first.

faqs.q: How is this different from Workflow Automation?
faqs.a: Workflow Automation focuses on SaaS and data connections. AI AUTOMATION centers on AI classify, draft, and summarize in the workflow.

faqs.q: Can you support tuning and expansion after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Prompt improvement, workflow expansion, and additional integrations can continue under separate agreement.
